title: Power Pages: environment-level governance of external authentication providers
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, admin paths, default state and enforcement warnings are supported. Licensing and automation gaps remain unconfirmed by Microsoft documentation after targeted searches; the authentication targeting labels need only a minor wording correction.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns Power Pages external authentication provider governance.
claims.quote: Power Pages: Administration and governance - Manage external authentication providers with granular controls

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Administrators can restrict authentication options across sites in an environment.
claims.quote: Authentication governance gives you, as an admin, control over which authentication options makers can configure for Power Pages sites in your environments.

claims.claim: Environment-level governance permits site-specific exceptions.
claims.quote: All sites except specific sites | Makers can configure the option for every site except the sites you select.

claims.claim: The roadmap says makers will only see and select approved identity providers.
claims.quote: Makers will only see and select from the approved IDPs when setting up authentication, ensuring consistent governance and alignment with enterprise security policies.

claims.claim: Learn says a blocked protocol or provider appears dimmed in the design studio.
claims.quote: In the design studio, a protocol or identity provider that governance blocks appears dimmed and can't be configured.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Makers cannot configure a blocked authentication option.
claims.quote: Makers can configure an option only when that option and all its parent controls are allowed for the site.

claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: all authentication options are allowed by default unless administrators configure restrictions.
claims.quote: By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure. No action is required unless your organization wants to restrict the options available to makers.

claims.claim: Previously configured tenant external-authentication restrictions are preserved.
claims.quote: If you set an external-authentication control for your tenant before environment-level granular governance was introduced, that setting is preserved.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing preserved restrictions for each environment.
claims.quote: Review it for each environment to confirm that it still matches your intent.

Opened external-auth-control, REST Websites, pac admin/pages/power-pages and Power Apps Administration PowerShell reference.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for non-production public-access governance.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages non-production site visibility governance Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin public access environment. Opened site-visibility-governance, REST Websites, pac admin/pages/power-pages and PowerShell module reference; site visibility operations govern a different setting.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing requirements have not been published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance external-auth-control licensing Managed Environments meter; Power Pages licensing authentication governance controls Managed Environments requirements. Opened external-auth-control, Power Platform licensing FAQs and Managed environments overview.

claims.claim: No feature-specific authentication-governance meter has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance external-auth-control licensing Managed Environments meter. Opened external-auth-control and Power Platform licensing FAQs; the latter documents website visitor meters, not an authentication-governance meter.

claims.claim: A Managed Environments dependency for authentication governance has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages licensing authentication governance controls Managed Environments requirements. Opened external-auth-control, Power Platform licensing FAQs and Managed environments overview; none states this control requires Managed Environments.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk, impact
claims.claim: Blocking an authentication option can stop users signing in to existing live sites through that option.
claims.quote: When a governance setting that blocks an authentication option takes effect, users can no longer sign in or register by using that authentication option.

claims.claim: An authentication governance block takes precedence over existing maker configuration.
claims.quote: If an existing site configuration uses a sign-in method associated with a blocked option, the governance setting takes precedence.

claims.claim: The authentication-governance Learn page does not specify the exact administrator role required.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance Purview audit role administrator. Read external-auth-control in full: it addresses admins and gives configuration steps, but names no required security role.

claims.claim: Tenant administrators configure non-production public-access governance.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can control whether makers can make a Power Pages site public when either the site or its environment is non-production.

claims.claim: Whether this specific authentication governance control is audited in Purview remains an open question.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance Purview audit role administrator. Opened external-auth-control and activity-logs-power-pages; the audit table names anonymous-access governance but does not identify this authentication-governance control.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents the authentication governance control even though its roadmap status remains In development.
